title: Assault with corrosive chemicals or flammable substances
summary: Willfully and maliciously placing or throwing a listed corrosive acid, caustic chemical or flammable substance on another person, with intent to injure the flesh or disfigure the body. The statute defines flammable substances; this is not every chemical exposure.
penalty: Felony: 2, 3, or 4 years in state prison. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful and malicious conduct with intent to injure or disfigure.

title: Assault with a stun gun or less lethal weapon
summary: An assault on another person using a stun gun or a less lethal weapon as defined by Penal Code section 16780. Assault requires an unlawful attempt and present ability to apply violent force; completed injury is not required.
penalty: Felony: 16 months, 2 years, or 3 years under section 1170(h); misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful act with awareness of facts that would lead a reasonable person to realize it would directly and probably result in force; present ability is required. Intent to injure is not required.

title: Stun-gun assault on a peace officer or firefighter
summary: Assault with a stun gun or statutory less lethal weapon on a peace officer or firefighter performing their duties, when the accused knows or reasonably should know that status and duty. The protected status and lawful-duty requirements matter.
penalty: Felony: 2, 3, or 4 years under section 1170(h); misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful act with awareness of facts that would lead a reasonable person to realize it would directly and probably result in force; present ability is required. Intent to injure is not required. The specified knowledge or reason to know victim status and duty is also required.

title: Aggravated assault on a transit operator or passenger
summary: Assault with a deadly weapon or instrument, or force likely to produce great bodily injury, on a covered transit operator, driver, passenger, station agent or ticket agent. The statute requires the specified duty or passenger status and knowledge or reason to know it.
penalty: Felony: 3, 4, or 5 years in state prison. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful act with awareness of facts that would lead a reasonable person to realize it would directly and probably result in force; present ability is required. Intent to injure is not required. The specified knowledge or reason to know victim status and duty is also required.

title: Aggravated assault on a custodial officer
summary: Assault with a deadly weapon or instrument, or means likely to produce great bodily injury, on a custodial officer defined by section 831 or 831.5 who is performing their duties, with knowledge or reason to know that status.
penalty: Felony: 3, 4, or 5 years in state prison. A qualifying weapon owned by the defendant may also be confiscated and destroyed. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful act with awareness of facts that would lead a reasonable person to realize it would directly and probably result in force; present ability is required. Intent to injure is not required. The specified knowledge or reason to know victim status and duty is also required.

title: Aggravated assault on a school employee
summary: Assault using a deadly weapon or instrument other than a firearm, or force likely to produce great bodily injury on a school employee performing their duties, when the accused knows or reasonably should know the employee’s status and duty. Section 245.5(d) defines covered employees; not every person on a campus qualifies.
penalty: Felony: 3, 4, or 5 years in state prison; misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful act with awareness of facts that would lead a reasonable person to realize it would directly and probably result in force; present ability is required. Intent to injure is not required. The specified knowledge or reason to know victim status and duty is also required.

title: Firearm assault on a school employee
summary: Assault using a firearm on a school employee performing their duties, when the accused knows or reasonably should know the employee’s status and duty. Section 245.5(d) defines covered employees; not every person on a campus qualifies.
penalty: Felony: 4, 6, or 8 years in state prison; misdemeanor alternative: 6 months to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful act with awareness of facts that would lead a reasonable person to realize it would directly and probably result in force; present ability is required. Intent to injure is not required. The specified knowledge or reason to know victim status and duty is also required.

title: Stun-gun or taser assault on a school employee
summary: Assault using a stun gun or taser on a school employee performing their duties, when the accused knows or reasonably should know the employee’s status and duty. Section 245.5(d) defines covered employees; not every person on a campus qualifies.
penalty: Felony: 2, 3, or 4 years in state prison; misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful act with awareness of facts that would lead a reasonable person to realize it would directly and probably result in force; present ability is required. Intent to injure is not required. The specified knowledge or reason to know victim status and duty is also required.

title: Hazing without resulting serious bodily injury
summary: Engaging in student initiation or preinitiation likely to cause serious bodily injury, where no serious bodily injury results. Customary athletic events and school-sanctioned events are excluded by the statutory definition.
penalty: Misdemeanor: a $100 to $5,000 fine, up to 364 days in county jail, or both. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Engaging in conduct meeting the statutory hazing definition.

title: Hazing resulting in serious bodily injury or death
summary: Personally engaging in statutory hazing that causes death or serious bodily injury. The initiation must meet section 245.6(b), and serious bodily injury is defined by section 243(f)(4); ordinary participation in an organization alone is not this offense.
penalty: Felony: 16 months, 2 years, or 3 years under section 1170(h); misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. The felony term comes from section 1170(h)(1), not a degree assigned to hazing. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Personal engagement in statutory hazing resulting in the specified harm.

title: Shooting at an inhabited dwelling or occupied vehicle
summary: Maliciously and willfully firing at an inhabited dwelling, occupied building, occupied motor vehicle or aircraft, or an inhabited housecar or camper. Inhabited means currently used as a dwelling, even if nobody is inside at that moment.
penalty: The statute calls the offense a felony and provides 3, 5, or 7 years in state prison, with a 6-month to 364-day county-jail alternative. Section 17 governs when misdemeanor treatment is available. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Malicious and willful discharge at a qualifying target.

title: Grossly negligent discharge of a BB device
summary: Willfully discharging a BB device with gross negligence that could injure or kill a person, except as otherwise authorized by law. The statute covers devices expelling a projectile by air pressure, gas pressure or spring action.
penalty: Misdemeanor: up to 364 days in county jail. The firearm felony alternative in subdivision (a) does not apply to this BB-device branch. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful discharge and gross negligence.

title: Shooting at an unoccupied aircraft
summary: Willfully and maliciously discharging a firearm at an unoccupied aircraft. Section 247 defines aircraft as a contrivance intended and capable of transporting persons through airspace.
penalty: Felony: section 247(a) states no term, so section 18(a) supplies 16 months, 2 years, or 3 years in state prison. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful and malicious discharge.

title: Shooting at an unoccupied vehicle or uninhabited building
summary: Discharging a firearm at an unoccupied motor vehicle or an uninhabited building or dwelling. The subdivision excludes shooting at the listed targets with the owner’s permission. This branch must not be confused with shooting at inhabited or occupied targets under section 246.
penalty: Felony: 16 months, 2 years, or 3 years in state prison under section 18(a); misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Discharge at the specified target; the owner-permission exception and applicable mental-state instructions require attention.

title: Malicious laser discharge at an occupied aircraft
summary: Willfully and maliciously discharging a laser at an occupied aircraft, whether moving or in flight. The statutory laser definition requires output exceeding one milliwatt continuous wave. Specified United States Armed Forces laser-development activity is excluded.
penalty: Misdemeanor: up to 364 days in county jail or a $1,000 fine. Felony: 16 months, 2 years, or 3 years under section 1170(h), or a $2,000 fine. These are the section’s stated alternatives, not an automatic combination of fine and custody. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful and malicious discharge.

title: Shining a bright light to interfere with an aircraft
summary: Willfully shining a light or other bright device at an aircraft, with intent to interfere with its operation, where the intensity is capable of impairing aircraft operation. Mere possession of a light is not this offense.
penalty: Misdemeanor: up to 364 days in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Willful shining with intent to interfere with aircraft operation.

title: Making a forged driver’s license or identification card
summary: Altering, falsifying, forging, duplicating, reproducing or counterfeiting a government-issued driver’s license or identification card with intent that it facilitate forgery. Possessing false identification for an unrelated purpose does not by itself establish this specific charge.
penalty: Felony: 16 months, 2 years, or 3 years under section 1170(h); misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Intent that the identification be used to facilitate forgery.

title: Possessing or displaying identification to facilitate forgery
summary: Displaying, allowing display of, or possessing a forged or altered driver’s license or identification card of the type described in section 470a with intent that it facilitate forgery. Possessing false identification for an unrelated purpose does not by itself establish this specific charge.
penalty: Felony: 16 months, 2 years, or 3 years under section 1170(h); misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Intent that the identification be used to facilitate forgery.

title: Fraudulent alteration or creation of a medical record
summary: Altering or modifying someone’s medical record, or creating a false medical record, with fraudulent intent. An innocent correction or clerical mistake is not enough.
penalty: Misdemeanor. Because section 471.5 states no special punishment, section 19 supplies up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Additional fines, restitution, assessments and applicable enhancements require separate review.
mentalState: Fraudulent intent.

title: Battery causing serious bodily injury
summary: Willful and unlawful use of force or violence on another person that causes serious bodily injury. Section 243(f)(4) defines that injury as a serious impairment of physical condition and gives examples; do not automatically equate every injury with this branch.
penalty: Felony: 2, 3, or 4 years under section 1170(h); misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Applicable enhancements, restitution and assessments require separate review.
mentalState: Willful and unlawful force; resulting serious bodily injury.

title: Assault with a firearm

penalty: Felony: 2, 3, or 4 years in state prison; misdemeanor alternative: 6 months to 364 days in county jail. A fine up to $10,000 may accompany imprisonment. A qualifying weapon owned by the defendant must be confiscated and disposed of under section 245(e). Section 17 governs misdemeanor treatment. These are adult base penalties, not a prediction of the total sentence. Applicable enhancements, restitution and assessments require separate review.
